ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an 8×8 black-and-white alternating chessboard; the white square in the 6th column from the left in the bottom row is labeled P, the white square in the 7th column from the left in the top row is labeled Q, and the figure also uses circles to draw an example path moving diagonally upward row by row. Reasoning: Each step must move to an adjacent white square in the row above, so the column number can only change by -1 or +1 each step, denoted respectively as L and R. From column 6 of P to column 7 of Q, the net column change after 7 steps is +1, so if the boundary is not considered, 4 R and 3 L are needed, with a total of C(7,4)=35 sequences. Since the starting point is in column 6 and there are only 3 L, it is impossible to cross the left boundary; the only possible illegality is reaching column 9, that is, crossing the right boundary. Illegal sequences are those in which, in some prefix, R exceeds L by 3. If the first arrival at column 9 occurs on step 3, then the first three steps must be RRR, and in the remaining 4 steps place 1 R and 3 L, giving 4 kinds; if it first occurs on step 5, then the first 5 steps have 4 R and 1 L, and step 5 is R, so the single L must be in the first 3 positions, giving 3 kinds. There are 4+3=7 illegal sequences in total. Therefore the number of legal paths is 35-7=28.
